analysis:
The PR replaces the single-threaded read-then-hash loop in WeightHasher.hashSingleFileUncached with OverlappedFileDigest. This is a new class that uses a dedicated reader thread and two 4 MiB page-aligned buffers, read with pread at explicit offsets. The PR also updates the tests and docs. It affects the weight-integrity hash path, which feeds catalog weight_hash verification (relevant to A-004, T-012 and T-027).

I traced the handoff protocol in OverlappedFileDigest.swift (lines 48-88). Both free semaphores are signaled at start. The reader waits on free[slot], preads, stores the length, signals filled[slot], and exits on count<=0. The hasher waits on filled[slot] and hashes exactly `count` bytes in order. It returns nil if count<0, so read errors never produce a partial digest; the nil falls back to the existing readers and ultimately fails closed. Short preads are handled because the offset advances by the actual count. EINTR is retried. The defer waits on readerExited, so the caller's close() in WeightHasher.swift (lines 253-256) only runs after the reader has stopped. lengths[] is visible across threads because the semaphore handoffs give happens-before ordering. Each buffer slot is written by only one side at a time, so there is no buffer race. Semaphore final values are at or above their initial value of 0, so there is no libdispatch trap on deallocation. The digest is the same SHA-256 over the same bytes, and the per-file digest combination in hashFilesWithRelativeKey is unchanged.

Memory use is bounded: 8 MiB per file, so about 32 MiB at the 4-worker maximum. Each file adds one short-lived thread, and the Thread is not retained after exit. Tests add chunk-boundary cases (including two and three chunks to exercise buffer wrap), page-stamped payloads that distinguish chunk order, and a concurrent-readers test. I found no authorization, encryption, attestation or data-exposure changes. The docs change only describes the new reader. T-041 (KV cache) is not touched. No security regression identified; the native-Apple runtime behavior of F_NOCACHE with pread was not verifiable from the supplied text, but a failure there falls back to the existing readers.
